title: Cardiac Muscle-cell Based Actuator and Self-stabilizing Biorobot - PART 1
protocol: Calculate the mass of PDMS needed using equation (1).
Use a ratio of 10:1 base to curing agent by weight for PDMS.
Estimate the mass of PDMS required for a specific height (5 mm) for the base of the biological actuator.
Calculate the mass of Ni-PDMS needed using equation (1).
Use ratios of 1:1.88 and 1:1.71:0.171 for Nickel Powder to PDMS, and Nickel Powder to PDMS Base to PDMS curing agent by weight respectively.
Estimate the mass of Ni-PDMS required for a specific height (1.5 mm) of the bottom base of the biorobot.
Check the dynamic stability of the biorobot with the desired dimension and geometry using analysis scripts.
Spin-coat a thin film of PDMS.
Place a silicon wafer on a photoresist spinner.
Flip the pump switch on to produce suction.
Pour positive photoresist onto the silicon wafer until the wafer is completely covered.
Program the spinner to spin at 2,000 rpm for 20 s.
Engage the spinner by pressing on the foot pedal.
Turn off the suction after spinning.
Heat a hot plate up to 120 °C.
Use wafer tweezers to pick up the silicon wafer from the spinner and place it directly on the hotplate.
Cover the wafer with a shallow petri dish and bake for 10 min.
Place a plastic container on a weighing scale and zero it out.
Pour 6 g of PDMS base into the container.
Add 0.6 g of PDMS curing agent to the container.
Mix the PDMS thoroughly for 5 min.
Place the container of mixed PDMS into a vacuum chamber.
Reduce the pressure of the vacuum chamber to 100 mbar.
Leave the container in the chamber for 30 min.
Break the vacuum and remove the container.
Keep the container covered until use.
Place the silicon wafer with the baked photoresist layer on the spinner.
Slowly pour the entire degassed PDMS mixture onto the wafer.
Set the spinner to 1,200 rpm for 5 min.
Turn on the spinner suction and engage the spinner.
Turn off the suction after spinning.
Heat an oven to 40 °C.
Pick up a silicon wafer from the spinner using wafer tweezers.
Place the wafer in the heated oven.
Bake the wafer overnight.
Cool the wafter at room temperature.
Turn on the power switch of the laser engraver and its exhaust.
Connect to the computer linked with the laser engraver.
Open the laser engraver software.
Select "File" option, then open the biological actuator design file.
Press the "Settings" button.
Change the power setting for blue to 3% and speed to 4%, then click “Set”.
Click on "Black", change mode to skip, then click “Set”.
Repeat settings for red color.
Press the "Apply" button.
Activate the engraver button at top right.
Press the "Relocate" button to center the design in software screen.
Focus view by clicking on edge of biorobot in the program.
Manually move the wafer with tweezers under guiding laser dot.
Start engraving the prior job.
Remove the wafer after engraving is complete.
Turn off all equipment.
Pour glass beads into a 15 mL tube.
Immerse the beads with 70% ethanol in DI water for 24 h.
Remove the ethanol and fill the tube with DI water for 24 h.
Pour out the DI water and place the tube on a hotplate at 50 °C to facilitate drying of the glass beads.
Add 3 g to the amount of PDMS found in equation (1) to account for PDMS that will stick to container sides during pouring.
Use equation (2) to find PDMS base and curing agent amounts.
Place a plastic container on a weighing scale and zero it out.
Pour the amount of PDMS base into the container and zero it out.
Then pour the amount of PDMS curing agent into the container.
Mix the PDMS thoroughly for 5 min.
Place a container on a scale and zero out.
Pour the correct amount of PDMS from step 2.3.2 into the container.
Drop cleaned glass beads throughout the PDMS mixture at regular intervals, ensuring 5 mm space around each bead.
Place the container in a vacuum chamber.
Reduce the vacuum pressure to 100 mbar and turn off the vacuum pump.
Break the vacuum after 30 minutes and remove the container.
Cover the container until use.
Heat a hotplate to 40 °C.
Carefully place the container of PDMS and glass beads on the hot plate.
Cover the container and bake overnight.
Cut cubes (5 mm x 5 mm x 5 mm) out of the bulk PDMS using a razor blade, ensuring one bead is in the center of each cube.
Clean all sides of each biological actuator base by pressing into tape to remove contaminants.
Repeat cleaning for each side.
Heat a hotplate to 40 °C.
Place the silicon wafer with the assemblies on the hot plate.
Cover the wafer and bake overnight.
Use tweezers to place the cleaned cube from step 2.4.2 on the base area that is covered with liquid PDMS.
Repeat steps involving placing a drop of liquid PDMS, smearing it, and attaching the cube for each device.
Spin-coat and laser-engrave a thin PDMS film using a new silicon wafer.
Use a biorobot design for laser engraving instead of the biological actuator design previously used.
Pour phenolic microballoons into a 50 mL tube until full.
Fill the tube with 70% ethanol in DI-water and let it sit for 24 h.
Pour out the ethanol, add DI water, and let it sit for 24 h.
Pour out the DI water, and place the tube on a hotplate at 50 °C to facilitate drying before use.
Use equation (1) with MB-PDMS density and 3.5 mm height to find volume of PDMS required.
Add 3 g to total amount for material remaining in container after pouring.
Use equation (3) to find PDMS base and curing agent amounts.
Measure appropriate amount of PDMS base, curing agent, and microballoons using scale.
Mix MB-PDMS mixture for 5 min.
Carefully pour calculated amount of MB-PDMS into a container using a scale.
Reduce vacuum chamber pressure to 100 mbar for 30 min.
Break the vacuum and remove container; keep covered until use.
Use equation (1) with Ni-PDMS density and 1.5 mm height to find volume of PDMS needed.
Add 3 g to total amount as in previous step.
Use equation (2) to find PDMS base and curing agent amounts.
Measure appropriate amount of PDMS base, curing agent, and nickel powder using scale.
Mix Ni-PDMS mixture for 5 min.
Carefully pour calculated amount of Ni-PDMS into a container using a scale.
Reduce vacuum chamber pressure to 100 mbar for 30 min.
Break the vacuum and remove container; keep covered until use.
Heat a hotplate to 40 °C.
Place containers with MB-PDMS and Ni-PDMS on the hot plate.
Cover each container.
Bake overnight.
Cut biorobot bases from Ni-PDMS using a razor blade.
Clean all sides of the biorobot bases by pressing into tape and removing.
Turn on a corona discharger.
Bring the tip of the corona discharger 1 cm above the Ni-PDMS base placed on a metal plate with a cleanroom tissue in between.
Move the tip around the base for 15 s to treat the surface.
Treat the surface of the biorobot engraved base for 15 s using the same method.
Place the Ni-PDMS treated side onto the treated side of the film.
Let the device sit for 5 min.
Use sharp tweezers to peel the biorobot cantilever from the wafer and place it on the bottom of the Ni-PDMS base.
Place a small drop of uncured PDMS (10:1 base to curing agent) on the top of the MB-PDMS base.
Use tweezers to place the side of the Ni-PDMS with the thin film PDMS on the MB-PDMS with the uncured PDMS.
Place the assembly in a plastic petri dish, and then place this on a hotplate at 40 °C to cure overnight.
Prepare fibronectin solution (50 µg/mL).
Place 100 µL of fibronectin solution into the center of a T-25 culture flask.
Place the biorobot or biological actuator facing down over the droplet of fibronectin solution.
Ensure that the cantilever is unfolded and immersed within the droplet.
Incubate at 37 ℃ for 30 min.
Remove the fibronectin solution after incubation.
Wash with PBS twice.
Remove the PBS.
Fill the flask with 10 mL of DMEM complete.
Incubate at 37 ℃ for 1 h to facilitate degassing of the PDMS.
Use a magnet to hold the device at the bottom of the flask, submerging it in 10 mL of media.
Place the flask with the samples in an ultrasonication bath for 5 min to remove bubbles.
